description: The Earth Snake in Chinese astrology: personality, Earth element traits, 1929 and 1989 dates and compatibility.
answer: In Chinese astrology, the Earth Snake is the Snake born in a Earth year, one of five versions of the sixth animal. It combines the Snake's insight with Earth's qualities. Earth Snake years between 1924 and 2044 are 1929 and 1989. The Snake's fixed element is Fire.

sections.heading: The Earth Snake personality
paragraphs: The Earth Snake is often described as the most grounded and approachable member of its sign. Fire generates Earth in the five-element cycle, and the Snake's fixed element is Fire, so the animal pours its warmth into the year element, producing a calm, practical and reliable character. Earth Snakes tend to be patient, thoughtful and good at managing resources, with a steady approach to long-term plans. They are frequently portrayed as loyal friends with a quiet sense of humour. The outward flow of energy makes them generous with time and care, but it can also leave them drained, and their caution may make them slow to embrace change or new people.

Earth sits at the centre of the five-element wheel, and an Earth year is traditionally said to give any animal steadiness, patience and a practical turn of mind. Descriptions associate it with reliability, honesty and a talent for holding things together, whether that means a family, a budget or a team in a difficult season. Earth-year people are often portrayed as grounded, fair and good at turning ideas into workable plans. The element is linked with nourishment and care, so it carries a quiet generosity. Its shadow, in most readings, is heaviness: worry, stubbornness and a reluctance to move until every risk has been weighed twice.

sections.heading: Earth Snake at work and in love
paragraphs: At work, Earth is usually associated with management, organisation and long-term stewardship. Earth-year people are often described as the steady hands who keep systems running, look after budgets and notice when colleagues are struggling, which suits administration, property, finance, agriculture, healthcare and operations. They tend to earn trust slowly and keep it. The traditional caution is resistance to change: an Earth stem may hold on to a process after it has stopped working, so regular reviews and a willingness to experiment help.

Calm under pressure and wise about money, the Earth Snake is cast as the steady counsel behind successful ventures. Accountancy, wealth management, property, estate planning and senior administration are frequently mentioned. It moves carefully, checks every clause and rarely makes the same mistake twice, so employers who reward discretion and long service tend to keep it for years. To a spouse or close friend, the Earth Snake offers composure, loyalty and practical security, plus a dry wit reserved for intimates. It wants stability and somebody who respects privacy. The common complaint from loved ones is slowness to open up: affection appears in deeds, while verbal reassurance can feel rationed.

sections.heading: Earth Snake years and dates
paragraphs: Earth Snake years in the Lunar New Year table run from February 10, 1929 to January 29, 1930 and from February 6, 1989 to January 26, 1990. Because the year begins at Lunar New Year, a birthday in January or early February needs checking: in 1929 anyone born before Feb 10 is a Earth Dragon, not a Earth Snake. Sixty years separate each Earth Snake year, the length of a full round of five elements and twelve animals. Every Earth Snake year is Yin, matching the Snake's own polarity.

Its traditional name is Ji-Si: Ji is the yin Earth stem and Si is the Snake's branch. Births just before each new year fall in the Earth Dragon year (before February 10, 1929) and the Earth Dragon year (before February 6, 1989), and births in the weeks after each Earth Snake year ends belong to the Metal Horse. The new year itself fell on a Sunday in 1929 and Monday in 1989.

sections.heading: Growth edges and compatibility for the Earth Snake
paragraphs: For the Earth Snake, small, regular risks are usually more useful than waiting for the perfect moment. Trying new activities and meeting new people keeps their natural caution from narrowing their world. Because they give steadily to others, they also need to replenish their own energy; scheduled rest and creative pleasures help. Earth Snakes may hold on to grievances quietly, so addressing hurt directly protects friendships. Practical goals such as building savings or developing a skill suit their patient nature. When steadiness and insight come together, the Earth Snake becomes a calm, trusted advisor.

For relationships, the classical structures belong to the animal rather than the element, so the Earth Snake shares the Snake's San He trine with the Ox and Rooster (the Metal trine), its Liu He bond with the Monkey, and its Liu Chong clash with the Pig. The element adds a second layer: another Earth sign shares this year element, while partners whose year element feeds Earth in the generating cycle are often described as supportive.

faq.question: What years are Earth Snake years?
faq.answer: Between 1924 and 2044: 1929 (from February 10, 1929) and 1989 (from February 6, 1989). Each lasts until the day before the next Lunar New Year.

faq.question: What is the Earth Snake's element relationship?
faq.answer: The year element is Earth and the Snake's fixed element is Fire; in the five-element cycles fire generates Earth. Readings use that relationship to describe how easily the two sides of the sign sit together.

faq.question: Which animals are most compatible with the Earth Snake?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Ox and Rooster (San He) and the Monkey (Liu He). The Pig is the Liu Chong clash. These pairings depend on the animal, whatever the element.

faq.question: What is the Earth Snake called in the Chinese calendar?
faq.answer: Ji-Si. In almanacs and Four Pillars charts each year is named by its heavenly stem, here the Earth stem Ji, followed by its earthly branch, here Si for the Snake, so the name pins down both halves of the combination at once.

faq.question: How is the Earth Snake different from other Snakes?
faq.answer: All Snakes share insight, poise and quiet determination. The Earth year element changes the tone: earth sits at the centre of the five-element wheel, and an Earth year is traditionally said to give any animal steadiness, patience and a practical turn of mind.
